active.title: Drop the dead Java 17 JVM options from the Spark Arrow path
active.description: On Temurin 17 with pyspark 3.5.8 the three Arrow tests pass without the extraJavaOptions netty reflection flag and java.nio --add-opens, because Spark's launcher adds the opens itself (the 0.8.1 PLAN M4 failure was Java 21). Design: amend the 0.8.1 AC2.8 contract that requires the options; delete them (and their comment) from the session builder in tests/fixtures/f2_spark_generator_specs_right.py; delete the netty sentence from rand_engine/cases/databricks.py.txt and docs/tutorials/databricks.md. Also: the databricks starter sets spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled on the shared session-wide test Spark session and nothing resets it, so the Spark tests depend on order (tests/test_9_cli.py runs the starter); the test that runs the starter restores the conf, or runs it on an isolated session.

active.title: Text generation performance follow-ups after the Arrow rewrite
active.description: (1) dates with time directives is only ~1.2x faster than 0.8.0 (7.71 s -> 6.28 s at 10M rows, measured in J3.T6) against ~25x for date-only, because each time field runs per-row digit loops; candidate: a two-digit pair table per field, as int_zfilled already does; 0.8.1 AC1.3 covered date-only only. (2) uuid4 in rand_engine/core/_np_core.py hex-encodes through bytes.hex().encode(), ~640 MB of temporaries at 10M rows; binascii.hexlify writes the hex bytes directly. (3) zero-row uuid4 and int_zfilled now return an empty Arrow column (0.8.0: empty float64, and a raise) and no test pins it; add the zero-size partition to their contract tests.

active.title: One shared virtualenv for the repo's verify gate
active.description: The verify: line in the repo AGENTS.md sets POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_IN_PROJECT=false with one shared poetry cache, so poetry builds a ~0.66 GB virtualenv per worktree path and nothing removes it when the tree is dropped; on 2026-10-20 70 orphaned environments (43 GB) filled the disk. Design: one shared environment that every tree's verify: reuses (for example POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_CREATE=false inside one environment kept under the shared cache), not one per path. This changes the verify: gate, so the operator rules on it with its measured cost per run against the current line (a cold and a warm run of each).
active.provenance: operator ruling on the 0.8.1 intake report, 2026-10-20; operations finding 2026-10-20 (disk full from per-worktree verify environments)

active.title: Compatibility release for the Python, pandas, pyarrow and Faker versions in use
active.description: Horizon: short. Operator answer (verbatim): "Cobrir o que está em uso (Recomendado)". Outcome: rand-engine installs beside the libraries in use today: Python 3.11-3.14 (3.10 EOL 2026-10-01), pandas >=2.2,<4, a pyarrow floor that fits Databricks 17.3 LTS (pyarrow 19.0.1) with no major cap, Faker uncapped; CI keeps 12 legs (one pandas 2.2 leg, the rest pandas 3.x; Spark 3.5 and 4.x). Evidence (inspection): 0.8.0 requires pandas<3.0.0, pyarrow<24.0.0, faker<29.0.0, and uv pip compile proves rand-engine==0.8.0 with pandas>=3, pyarrow>=24 or faker>=30 unsatisfiable; current pandas 3.1.0, pyarrow 26.0.0, Faker 40.43.0, pyspark 4.2.0 (PyPI: pyspark 4.2.0/4.1.x declare pandas>=2.2.0, 4.0.x >=2.0.0, 3.5.8 none; https://pypi.org/pypi/pyspark/4.2.0/json). The registered HIGH bug dates-before-1970-validate-then-raise is fixed in this release (operator: "Confirmo, HIGH, já (Recomendado)"). It follows the 0.8.1 publish (operator: "Publicar 0.8.1 já (Recomendado)"). Version 0.9.0 is an agent default the operator has not ruled (minor: drops Python 3.10 and refuses the Spark dummy methods). Out of scope: Python 3.10, CI legs beyond the 12, any new feature or runtime dependency.

active.title: Mandatory hardware study: chunk size vs speed and peak memory, presented before any implementation
active.description: Horizon: medium, first (agent default order, unruled: study -> output/memory -> stream -> public benchmark -> docs -> JSON Schema + generate -> 1.0). Operator answer (verbatim): "devemos fazer em pedaços, mas devemos observar e fazer um estudo serio sobre o trade-off de velocidade vs montar em pedaçõ e fazer append, se usamos o disco, como usamos, quais seriam os chunks otimizados para que mantenhamos a velocidade e reduzimos. ... é obrigatorio vc me apresentar esse estudo ... um grafico onde temos eixos com o tamanho do chunk e a velocidade ... pelo menos 3 estrategias ... Oferecer como default memoria máxima consumida de 1GB. E usuário consegue passar alterar, diminuir, isso afetará no tamanho de chunks, devemos ter as estimativas de velocidade de geração para aquele tamanho de chunk." Outcome: a study presented to the operator before any chunked-output implementation, naming the winning strategy and chunk size per memory budget: a chunk-size sweep 10^3..10^8 rows, x = chunk size, y = throughput (rows/µs, MB/s), a second panel with peak RSS; at least 3 strategies among monolithic, sequential chunks + append, multiprocessing parts, threads with per-block Generators, and Python 3.14 free-threaded if the ecosystem supports it; interfering variables isolated (cache sizes, column types, format/codec, row-group size, workers, per-chunk fixed cost, page cache, disk type); hardware measured (CPU, caches, RAM bandwidth, disk write); per-block Philox streams tested so seeds are independent of chunk size and thread count. Out of scope: changing the library's generation or writers; the study is the operator's decision input.

active.title: Output speed first under a bounded memory budget
active.description: Horizon: medium, after hardware-chunk-study. Operator answers (verbatim): "A saída primeiro (Recomendado)"; "Writers/stream + get_df recusa (Recomendado)"; "Docs + plan() + CLI local (Recomendado)"; "Oferecer como default memoria máxima consumida de 1GB. E usuário consegue passar alterar, diminuir, isso afetará no tamanho de chunks, devemos ter as estimativas de velocidade de geração para aquele tamanho de chunk." Outcome: output built from the study's winning strategy: a memory budget, default 1 GB and user-adjustable, sets the chunk size from the measured bytes/row table; writers and stream obey it; get_df refuses an estimated frame above it with the estimate in the message; max_memory=None disables it; parallel part writing, Arrow-direct Parquet/CSV, vectorized JSON; gen.plan(max_memory=...) returns chunk rows, expected peak and throughput without measuring; `rand-engine benchmark --max-memory 1GB` measures the user's machine (~1 min); the docs publish the study curves on reference hardware. The draw-order change is a seed-contract revision in its SPEC (invariant 4). Measured motivation (CI): columns 7-512 rows/µs vs CSV 3, Parquet 2.4, JSON 0.5, stream_dict 0.17 rows/µs. Out of scope: the stream rate contract (stream-rate-per-microbatch), text-method speed (text-perf-follow-ups), a native core, a new runtime dependency.
